entries.title: Faction auction goes live
changes: The Preference Split Auction now works in online games - its sealed bidding is live on the server.
Applied preference_split_sealed_bids plus two hardening follow-ups (revoke-then-grant on auction_sealed_bids, pinned search_path on preference_split_budget); all three verified against live objects.

entries.title: Faction auction at any player count
changes: The Preference Split Auction is no longer 4-player only - it works at every player count, with one picked faction per player.
Its bid budget now scales with the table: 20 points at 2 players, 30 at 3, 40 at 4, so each player pays about the same either way.

Removed the 4-player gate from the resolver, moveInit and the create-game option list; the default budget is now defaultPreferenceSplitBudget(players) = 10 per player, mirrored in preference_split_budget() server-side.

entries.title: Faction auction pricing
changes: In the Preference Split Auction the winner now always pays the faction's average price, even if that is more than they bid on it themselves.
Removed the min(average, ownBid) cap from resolvePreferenceSplitAuction and dropped the now-meaningless rawPayment field; reveal screen, in-app rules and docs updated.
userChanges: In the Preference Split Auction the winner now always pays the faction's average price, even if that is more than they bid on it themselves.

entries.title: Preference Split Auction
changes: New 4-player faction auction: secretly split a fixed pot of bid points across the four factions, everyone at once.
The winner of a faction pays the average of all four bids on it, and never more than they bid themselves.
New AuctionVariant.PreferenceSplit end to end - engine resolver, phase/command, sealed-bid table + RPCs, bid form, reveal screen and create-game option.
Bids are sealed server-side (auction_sealed_bids, RLS + reveal_sealed_bids), so no player can read another's split before the reveal.
userChanges: New 4-player faction auction: secretly split a fixed pot of bid points across the four factions, everyone at once.

entries.title: Minigames come offline too
changes: Chess, renju and ultimate tic-tac-toe now travel with a converted offline game: you get the real positions on the plane, not fresh boards
Minigame moves and resets you make offline are sent to the online board when you reconnect, and are never silently thrown away
In an offline copy you can only play your own colour in a minigame, just like online

New logic/offline-minigame-sync.ts records offline minigame play as an ordered op log (each op carrying its own previous/next position) and replays it through the existing move(previous, next) RPCs, whose staleness check detects a conflict without any extra divergence logic
A board with a pending op log is never refreshed from the online row until the log has gone up; unsent ops are handed back and re-queued rather than dropped
The hosted colour assignments and the viewer's user id are written into the copy so offline boards can enforce the designated-mover rule instead of falling back to pass-and-play

entries.title: Offline moves are never lost
changes: Moves you play in an offline copy are now sent up to the online game when you are back online, instead of being replaced by it
An offline copy is never rolled back to an older online state
You can only play your own seats in an offline copy, since nobody can move for another player

syncOfflineMirror refreshes a copy only from an online state strictly further along the same history (compareMoveHistories: none/same/behind/ahead/diverged); an ahead or diverged copy is never written over

planOfflineUpload replays offline-only moves against the online engine and returns the leading run that can be committed, stopping at a seat this account does not hold or a move the engine now rejects; hosted.ts sends that run one move at a time, re-planning after each commit
mirrorSeats is recorded on the copy and self-contained.ts applies the hosted seatToLock rule to it, so a mirrored game is no longer played hot-seat

entries.title: Hosted persistence repair
changes: Hosted games now repair stale move-count drift before the first turn save, preventing setup picks from snapping back to player 1.

entries.title: Hosted faction-pick persistence

entries.title: Hosted sync and lobby fixes
